## Your task: the (c3)/(c4) flattening brick — `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/SlicingFlatKernel.lean`

This is brick 1 of the G-4 chain (w4-g4-worksheet §3, the (c3)/(c4) table row; file plan §5). PURE COMMUTATIVE ALGEBRA — no curves, no schemes, no project geometry vocabulary. Goal: over a Noetherian ring R, for a linear map δ' : M → N between finite projective modules whose residue-field fibres have g-dimensional kernels in a suitably strong sense, conclude: ker δ' is finite projective of rank g (constant rankAtStalk g), M ⧸ ker δ' is flat (equivalently the image is flat / locally split), and N ⧸ range δ' is flat. This generalizes the ENDOMORPHISM-shaped Noetherian induction of `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/SlicingFlat.lean` (read it in full first — esp. `Module.Flat.mem_smul_top_of_apply_mem_smul_top` at :79 and `Module.Flat.of_surjective_exact_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective` at :268-275) to a map between two different modules.

## CRITICAL — the statement must be fixed before any proving (probe-first discipline)

The worksheet's table-row pin ("dim_κ ker(δ' ⊗ κ(p)) constant = g ⟹ conclusions") is UNDER-HYPOTHESIZED — counterexample: R = k[ε] (= k[X]/(X²), Noetherian local), M = N = R, δ' = multiplication by ε. Then ker(δ' ⊗ κ) = ker(0 : k → k) is 1-dimensional at the unique prime (constant g = 1), but ker δ' = (ε) ≅ k is NOT projective and R ⧸ ker δ' = k is NOT flat. So constant fibre-kernel dimension alone is false; an extra hypothesis is needed that rules out fibre kernels not witnessed by relative elements.

The likely-correct shape (design first, verify against the k[ε] guard, then prove): add a fibrewise-spanning hypothesis — a finitely generated submodule L ≤ ker δ' (or ker δ' itself with a surjectivity clause) such that for every prime p, the image of L ⊗ κ(p) → M ⊗ κ(p) is ALL of ker(δ' ⊗ κ(p)), with dim_κ(p) ker(δ' ⊗ κ(p)) = g constant. (In the k[ε] guard this fails: elements of (ε) map to 0 in the fibre.) Equivalently you may find the cleanest form via the rTensor-residueField-injectivity criterion the landed endomorphism lemma uses: coker flat ⟺ (im δ') ⊗ κ(p) → im(δ' ⊗ κ(p)) injective for all p — the spanning hypothesis is what supplies it. Conclusions to deliver (each a named keystone): (1) `N ⧸ range δ'` flat; (2) `M ⧸ ker δ'` flat (≅ range δ'); (3) `ker δ'` finite projective with `rankAtStalk = g` everywhere; (4) L = ker δ' (if you take the L form); (5) the base-change corollary: formation of ker δ' commutes with — at minimum — residue fields ((ker δ') ⊗ κ(p) ≅ ker(δ' ⊗ κ(p))), stated so the downstream consumer can use it.

The fibre input the consumer will have (from P-fib-N + the seed): every fibre kernel is g-dimensional AND is spanned by residue-field images of relative elements of a f.g. submodule of ker δ'. Design your hypothesis to consume exactly that. Keep the file free of any AlgebraicJacobian import except possibly SlicingFlat itself (mathlib + SlicingFlat only), so it elaborates light.

SEARCH mathlib HARD before proving anything: lean_local_search + lean_loogle + lean_leansearch for: flatness via rTensor injectivity (`Module.Flat.iff_rTensor_injective'`), residue-field fibre criteria, `Module.rankAtStalk` API, finite projective ⟺ finite presentation + flat (`Module.Projective` over Noetherian: `Module.finite_flat_iff_projective`-shaped lemmas), locally split submodules, `LinearMap.exists_...` fibre-rank semicontinuity, `Module.FinitePresentation`.
